docs.title: kraft-last-standing
docs.text:
kraft-last-standing recovers an Apache Kafka® cluster whose KRaft controller quorum has permanently lost a majority of its voters. It shrinks the voter set down to a single surviving controller, by appending VotersRecord control records to that controller's local copy of the metadata log while it is stopped. When the controller starts again, it is the only voter, elects itself leader, and the cluster can make progress again.

Caution

Recovery cements data loss. Anything that only existed on the lost nodes is gone, and this tool cannot bring it back. Only use it once it is verified that the lost voters cannot be recovered, and follow the runbook.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Since KIP-853, the set of voters in a dynamic KRaft quorum lives in the metadata log itself, as VotersRecord control records. Changing the voter set means committing a new VotersRecord, which requires a majority of the current voters. When a majority is permanently lost, the lost voters can only be removed with quorum, and quorum can only be restored by removing the lost voters. Stock Kafka tooling has no way out of that loop, so the cluster stays down.

The way out is an offline edit of the log, in the same family as formatting storage with an initial voter set. The blog post Never lose quorum in Apache Kafka® describes the approach and its consequences in depth.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
$ pip install --require-virtualenv kraft-last-standing

kraft-last-standing requires Python 3.12 or later, and runs on the hosts that store the metadata log, reading and writing its files directly. It doesn't connect to Kafka.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The tool has two commands, which the runbook puts in context.

  • kraft-last-standing probe reports how far local copies of the metadata log have progressed, so that recovery can start from the most progressed one. It only reads.
  • kraft-last-standing recover backs up the metadata log of a stopped controller, and then appends records that remove every other voter, one at a time.

The usage page documents both commands in detail.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: kraft-last-standing works with clusters on Kafka 3.9 or later that use a dynamic quorum, that is with kraft.version 1 or later. It is tested against Kafka 4.3.1. A static quorum has no VotersRecord in its log, so the tool refuses to modify it.

docs.title: Runbook: recovering from lost controller quorum
docs.text:
This runbook describes how to bring an Apache Kafka® cluster back online after its KRaft controller quorum has permanently lost a majority of its voters. For example, a cluster with three voters that has irrecoverably lost two of them.

Caution

This is a destructive operation that cements data loss. Before continuing, exhaust every other option of recovering the lost nodes, or of recovering only their __cluster_metadata-0 directories.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Raft, and with it KRaft, needs a majority of voters to make progress. In a dynamic quorum, the voter set is stored in the metadata log as VotersRecord control records, so removing the lost voters means committing a new VotersRecord, which needs the majority that was lost. The surviving controllers keep waiting for the lost voters, and the cluster can't create topics, change configuration or elect partition leaders.

The way out is to edit the log of one surviving controller while it is stopped, appending VotersRecord entries that demote every other voter, one at a time. When that controller starts again, it is the only voter, considers itself leader, and can commit again. The surviving nodes replicate the appended records, learn that they are no longer voters, and continue from there.

Losing a majority of voters almost always means losing data, and this procedure doesn't recover any. Metadata that only existed on the lost nodes is gone, and depending on replication factors and which replicas survived, so is partition data. The procedure restores availability, not integrity.

To lose as little as possible, recovery starts from the most progressed surviving copy of the metadata log, which can belong to a broker as well as to a controller. Brokers can't handle the metadata log moving backwards, for instance leader epochs decreasing, so the recovered log must contain every record that a surviving node has already seen. Everything after the end of that copy is lost for good.

The blog post Never lose quorum in Apache Kafka® covers this reasoning in more depth.

docs.title: Identification
docs.text:
All of the following must hold before starting.

  • The cluster runs in KRaft mode with a dynamic quorum, which requires Kafka 3.9 or later. Nodes in a dynamic quorum are configured with controller.quorum.bootstrap.servers instead of controller.quorum.voters. kraft-last-standing probe lists the voters of a dynamic quorum.
  • The metadata log doesn't make progress. The high-watermark attribute of the kafka.server:type=raft-metrics MBean has stopped increasing on all nodes, and kafka-metadata-quorum.sh --bootstrap-controller HOST:PORT describe --status fails or shows no leader.
  • The cause is that a majority of the voters is lost, and it's exhaustively verified that they can't be recovered.

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
The procedure, in short:

  1. Back up the metadata log of every surviving node.
  2. Find the most progressed copy of the metadata log.
  3. Stop every controller.
  4. Recover one controller, from the most progressed copy.
  5. Start only the recovered controller.
  6. Start the other surviving nodes.
  7. Add controllers until the quorum has its intended size again.

docs.title: 1. Back up the metadata log of every surviving node
docs.text: kraft-last-standing recover backs up the directory it modifies, but nothing else. Before starting, make a copy of the __cluster_metadata-0 directory of every surviving broker and controller, so that the state as it was before recovery is available should something go wrong.

docs.title: 2. Find the most progressed copy of the metadata log
docs.text:
Every broker and controller has a local copy of the metadata log, in a directory named __cluster_metadata-0. It lives in the directory configured with metadata.log.dir, or in the first entry of log.dirs when that isn't set. A node with process.roles=broker,controller has a single copy, shared by both roles.

Install kraft-last-standing on every surviving node, and probe its copy:

$ kraft-last-standing probe /var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0
/var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0
  node ID:      1
  last offset:  1621
  leader epoch: 5
  snapshot:     00000000000000001600-0000000005.checkpoint
  voters:       1, 2, 3

Probing only reads files. When gathering results programmatically, use --json for machine-readable output.

Warning

Make sure to probe every surviving node, brokers included. A node that is left out might hold the most progressed copy of the log.

The most progressed copy is the one to recover from. Compare copies the way Raft compares logs: the copy with the highest leader epoch is the most progressed, and among copies with the same leader epoch, the one with the highest last offset. A copy can have a higher last offset but a lower leader epoch than another, when it diverged from the others under an earlier leader. The records in its divergent tail were never committed. If several copies are equally progressed, prefer one that belongs to a controller.

  • If a controller has the most progressed copy, recover that controller.
  • If a broker has the most progressed copy, pick any surviving controller that is listed among the voters, and copy the broker's __cluster_metadata-0 directory to that controller's host. Copy it into a new directory, rather than over the controller's own. For example:
$ mkdir /var/tmp/broker-4
$ scp -r broker-4:/var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0 /var/tmp/broker-4/

Nothing appends to the metadata log while the quorum has no leader, so the copy is consistent even when the broker is running.

If probing fails with an error about failing to read a record batch, that copy of the log is corrupt. Leave it out, and recover from the most progressed of the other copies.

docs.title: 3. Stop every controller
docs.text:
Stop the Kafka process of every controller, including the one to recover. Also stop anything that would restart them, such as a systemd unit with Restart= set, or configuration management. When an operator such as Strimzi manages the cluster, pause its reconciliation, so that it doesn't restart or roll nodes during the procedure.

Brokers can keep running.

docs.title: 4. Recover one controller
docs.text:
On the controller chosen in step 2, run recover as the user that owns the Kafka data, or as root:

$ kraft-last-standing recover \
    --metadata-dir /var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0 \
    --backup-dir /var/backups/kafka

When recovering from a broker's copy, also pass the directory it was copied to:

$ kraft-last-standing recover \
    --metadata-dir /var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0 \
    --backup-dir /var/backups/kafka \
    --copy-log-from /var/tmp/broker-4/__cluster_metadata-0

The command reads the controller's node ID and directory ID from meta.properties, prints a plan, and asks for confirmation before modifying anything. Check that the plan keeps the intended voter, and that the last offset matches the one found in step 2. The usage page describes the options in detail.

docs.title: 5. Start only the recovered controller
docs.text:
Start the Kafka process of the recovered controller, and keep every other controller stopped. Verify that it is the only voter, and that it is the leader:

$ kafka-metadata-quorum.sh --bootstrap-controller controller-1:9093 describe --status

LeaderId should be the recovered controller's node ID, and CurrentVoters should only list that controller. The high watermark should increase again. Running brokers reconnect to the new leader, and show up as observers in the output of describe --replication.

docs.title: 6. Start the other surviving nodes
docs.text: Start the remaining surviving nodes, and undo whatever was paused in step 3. Surviving controllers that were demoted rejoin as observers.

docs.title: 7. Restore the size of the quorum
docs.text:
A single voter can't tolerate any failure, so add controllers until the quorum has its intended size again. Each new controller must be formatted without an initial voter set:

$ kafka-storage.sh format \
    --cluster-id CLUSTER_ID \
    --no-initial-controllers \
    --config controller.properties

The cluster ID is the cluster.id in meta.properties of any existing node. Start the new controller, and once it shows up as an observer, promote it to voter by running this on its host:

$ kafka-metadata-quorum.sh \
    --bootstrap-controller controller-1:9093 \
    --command-config controller.properties \
    add-controller

add-controller reads the node ID, the advertised listeners and the directory ID of the new controller from its configuration and meta.properties. The request times out until the new controller has caught up with the leader, so retry it until it succeeds.

Demoted controllers that survived can be promoted the same way, without formatting them again.

A lost voter can't be brought back by formatting new storage under its node ID. Kafka identifies each replica by its node ID together with the directory ID that formatting generates, so fresh storage is a new replica, even with the same node ID. Now that the lost voters are no longer in the voter set, a replacement node can reuse their node IDs, and join as a new voter with add-controller.

docs.title: How recovery works
docs.text: recover reads the log segments and the latest snapshot of the metadata directory, and combines them the way Kafka does on startup. It finds the last offset, the leader epoch of the last batch, and the most recent VotersRecord, which only exists in the snapshot once Kafka has deleted the segments that held it. It then writes one VotersRecord control batch per voter to remove, at the offsets following the last one, to a new log segment named after its first offset, like Kafka names the segments it rolls. Each record removes one voter, so every step changes the voter set by a single voter, like regular membership changes do. Before appending, it moves the controller to a newer epoch in quorum-state, without a leader or vote, so that the controller holds a new election when it starts, rather than resuming one from before the recovery.

docs.title: Rolling back
docs.text: The backup made by recover is a directory holding a copy of the metadata directory as it was before recovery, such as /var/backups/kafka/__cluster_metadata-0.20261001T144217Z/__cluster_metadata-0. To roll back, stop the controller, and replace its __cluster_metadata-0 directory with that copy. The copy has the modes of the original files, but is owned by the user that ran recover, so give it back to the user that runs Kafka when that was root.

docs.title: Snapshots ahead of the log
docs.text: Without --copy-log-from, recover only deletes log segments when the latest snapshot is ahead of the log, which happens when a controller crashes right after downloading a snapshot from the leader. Kafka deletes such segments on its next start. For Kafka to keep the batches the tool appends, the tool must delete the segments first, so that it can write the batches at the end of the snapshot, where Kafka continues the log. With the segments in place, batches written after them are deleted along with them when Kafka starts, and batches written at the end of the snapshot leave a gap in the log, which Kafka never produces.

docs.title: How a controller gets there
docs.text:
Controller 2 was offline for ten days. Meanwhile, the leader deleted old segments, and its log now starts at offset 9000. Controller 2 comes back and fetches from offset 4200, which the leader no longer has, so the leader answers with the ID of its latest snapshot, which holds the state up to offset 9499 in epoch 12. Controller 2 downloads the snapshot, renames it into place, and is killed before it deletes its own segments. Its metadata directory now holds:

00000000000000003000.log                    offsets 3000–3599
00000000000000003600.log                    offsets 3600–4199, last epoch 9
00000000000000009500-0000000012.checkpoint  state up to offset 9499, epoch 12

A follower renames a downloaded snapshot into place before it deletes its segments (KafkaRaftClient), and Kafka's startup code handles a crash in between:

When recovering, truncate fully if the latest snapshot is after the log end offset. This can happen to a follower when the follower crashes after downloading a snapshot from the leader but before it could truncate the log fully.

docs.title: What Kafka does on startup
docs.text:
A snapshot is ahead of the log when its epoch is higher than that of the last batch in the log, or the epochs are equal and the snapshot ends after the log does (truncateToLatestSnapshot). When it is, Kafka calls truncateFullyAndStartAt with the end offset of the snapshot, which deletes every segment, clears the leader epoch cache, and starts an empty segment at that offset. In the example, Kafka deletes both segments and continues the log at offset 9500.

The tool does the same before appending. It deletes the segments and leader-epoch-checkpoint, which Kafka rebuilds from the log, and writes the new batches at the end offset of the snapshot, in the epoch of the snapshot. The plan lists the deleted segments under segments to delete, and the backup taken before any change holds them.

This differs from the usual state, where a snapshot covers a prefix of the segments. Kafka only takes snapshots of offsets it has, and deletes the segments behind them later, once they exceed the retention settings. The tool deletes nothing in that state.

docs.title: Copying the log
docs.text: With --copy-log-from, the copied directory can be in the same state. The tool then leaves the old segments out of the copy, lists them under segments to skip, and deletes nothing from the source. It replaces the controller's own segments either way, which is what the option is for.

docs.title: How common it is
docs.text: A leader sends a snapshot to any follower that fetches from before the leader's log start offset, or with a last fetched epoch older than the leader's oldest snapshot (RaftLog). It also sends one to every follower that fetches from offset 0, once it has a snapshot other than the bootstrap one (KafkaRaftClient). Snapshot downloads are routine, but ending up in this state also takes a crash between the rename and the deletion, a window of a few file operations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Both commands take paths to __cluster_metadata-0 directories, the directory that holds a node's local copy of the metadata log. It lives in the directory configured with metadata.log.dir, or in the first entry of log.dirs when that isn't set. Brokers and controllers both have one, and a node with process.roles=broker,controller has a single copy shared by both roles.

Like Kafka, the commands combine the log segments with the latest snapshot. They read the voter set from the log, and fall back to the snapshot once Kafka has deleted the segments that held it. A log in a state that Kafka doesn't leave it in is refused, such as one whose segments start after offset 0 without a snapshot of the offsets before them.

A process that is killed while appending to the log can leave an incomplete batch at the end of the last segment, which Kafka truncates on startup. The commands read the log without it, and recover truncates it before appending, listing it in the plan under incomplete batch. A batch that is corrupt, or incomplete anywhere else, is refused, since Kafka would discard every batch after it.

The commands exit with status 0 on success, and status 1 when they fail or the operator aborts. Errors that abort an operation are detected before anything is modified.

docs.title: probe
docs.text:
kraft-last-standing probe [--json] METADATA_DIR [METADATA_DIR ...]

Reports the last offset, leader epoch, latest snapshot and voter set of each given copy of the metadata log, sorted with the most progressed first: by leader epoch, and then by last offset. It only reads files, and the node ID comes from meta.properties in the parent directory, when there is one.

$ kraft-last-standing probe /var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0
/var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0
  node ID:      1
  last offset:  1621
  leader epoch: 5
  snapshot:     00000000000000001600-0000000005.checkpoint
  voters:       1, 2, 3

--json outputs the same information as a JSON array, for gathering results from many hosts with a script. Fields that the text output describes as unknown or none are null.

$ kraft-last-standing probe --json /var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0
[
  {
    "directory": "/var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0",
    "node_id": 1,
    "last_offset": 1621,
    "leader_epoch": 5,
    "snapshot": "00000000000000001600-0000000005.checkpoint",
    "voter_ids": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: recover
docs.text:
kraft-last-standing recover
    --metadata-dir METADATA_DIR
    --backup-dir BACKUP_DIR
    [--node-id NODE_ID]
    [--copy-log-from METADATA_DIR]
    [--yes]

Shrinks the voter set down to the controller that owns --metadata-dir. The controller must be stopped. The command reads the latest VotersRecord, and appends one VotersRecord per voter to remove, each with one voter fewer than the previous, until only the kept voter remains.

Before modifying anything, the command prints its plan and asks the operator for confirmation:

Recovery plan
  metadata directory: /var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0
  backup destination: /var/backups/kafka/__cluster_metadata-0.20261001T144217Z
  last offset:        1621
  leader epoch:       5
  snapshot:           00000000000000001600-0000000005.checkpoint
  file to rewrite:    quorum-state, to epoch 6 without a leader or vote
  current voters:     1, 2, 3
  voter to keep:      1 (directory ID J8aAPcfLQt2bqs1JT_rMgQ)
  voters to remove:   3, 2, in this order
  new log segment:    /var/lib/kafka/data/__cluster_metadata-0/00000000000000001622.log
  offsets to append:  1622 to 1623
Modify the metadata log as described above? [y/N]

Run the command as the user that owns the log segments, or as root. Created files get the mode and owner of the existing segments.

When there already is an empty segment at the first offset to append, which Kafka creates when rolling a segment, the command writes to it, and the plan marks it as (existing, empty).

A controller that crashes right after downloading a snapshot from the leader can have a snapshot that is ahead of its log segments. Kafka then deletes the segments on startup, and continues the log from the end of the snapshot. The command does the same, and the plan lists the segments under segments to delete. Snapshots ahead of the log describes this state in detail.

Whenever the command deletes or replaces segments, it also deletes leader-epoch-checkpoint, which would otherwise keep the leader epochs of the deleted segments. Kafka rebuilds it from the log on startup.

The command also rewrites quorum-state, where Kafka keeps the controller's epoch, the leader it knows of, and the candidate it voted for. A controller that voted for itself restarts as a candidate in that epoch, and as the only voter, it wins it, even when another controller already led it. Nodes that followed the other leader then don't follow the recovered controller. To prevent this, the command moves the controller to the epoch after the newest one in quorum-state and in the log, without a leader or vote, so that it holds a new election in a newer epoch when it starts.

docs.title: --metadata-dir METADATA_DIR
docs.text: The __cluster_metadata-0 directory of the controller to recover.

docs.title: --backup-dir BACKUP_DIR
docs.text: The directory to back up the metadata directory into, before modifying it. The backup is a timestamped directory holding a copy of the whole metadata directory. Since the metadata log can contain credentials, only the owner of the backup can access it. The backup directory is created if missing, and must not be inside the metadata directory.

docs.title: --node-id NODE_ID
docs.text: The ID of the voter to keep. By default, this is the node.id in meta.properties, which kafka-storage.sh format writes to the parent of the metadata directory. The command then also verifies that the directory.id in meta.properties matches the directory ID registered for the voter, since the controller wouldn't consider itself a voter after recovery otherwise. When --node-id is given, meta.properties isn't read, and the directory ID isn't verified.

docs.title: --copy-log-from METADATA_DIR
docs.text:
Replace the log segments and snapshots of the metadata directory with copies of the log segments and latest snapshot in this __cluster_metadata-0 directory, before appending. Use this when another node, usually a broker, has a more progressed copy of the log than any surviving controller. Copy that node's metadata directory to the controller's host first, and point this option at the copy. Segments that the copied snapshot is ahead of are left out, and the plan lists them under segments to skip. Other files in the metadata directory, such as indexes, are kept, and Kafka rebuilds them on startup.

A broker that truncated its log while the cluster was first starting leaves the voter set out of its snapshots, because of a bug in Kafka. Once Kafka has deleted the segments from that time, its copy has no voter set, and the command refuses it. Copy the log of another node instead.

docs.title: --yes
docs.text: Don't ask for confirmation.
